text:
anya_privacy: Quick question — we just received a DSAR that targets embeddings derived from customer data. Request asks for full deletion across regions and snapshots. Can we delegate to the DSAR service account to run the erase, or do we need a manual keystore handoff? Legal wants an auditable proof-of-deletion (signed manifest).

mike_infra: We added that service-account last month. It can call the erase API but it doesn't have KMS decrypt rights by default. KMS IAM is separate — SA needs explicit keyAccess on each keystore key.

sara_sec: If we grant SA decrypt across keys we lose separation of duties. Prefer routing through keystore-proxy that performs decrypt/delete and emits an immutable audit entry.

mike_infra: Agreed. keystore-proxy supports token exchange and short-lived grants. It can call KMS on behalf of the SA and write an audit record. Example call: `curl -X POST https://keystore-proxy.internal/erase -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"subject_id":"sub-123","shards":["s3://r1/...","s3://r2/..."]}'`

tom_oncall: Is our audit-log retention long enough for legal? They sometimes ask to keep deletion proof for up to 7 years for compliance.

alex_legal: We need tamper-evident proof: signed deletion manifest + chain-of-custody for the signing key. We don't need raw data retained, but the manifest and signature must be preserved. If this requires a retention-exception for audit stores, we'll request it.

anya_privacy: Proposed plan: let SA trigger keystore-proxy. Proxy will perform KMS decrypt/delete of embedding shards, write a signed manifest to AuditDB, and forward an immutable copy to cold storage. Who owns implementing the signed manifest and signing process?

sara_sec: Security can own manifest schema and the signing verification. We want the proxy to sign manifests using an HSM-backed signing key so signatures are non-repudiable. Also we need to ensure audit logs are forwarded to an immutable store (GCS cold / WORM) and retention policy is adjustable via retention-exception workflow.

devops-bot: deploybot: keystore-proxy v2.7.1 deployed to prod in us-east-1 at 2026-03-20T18:22Z :rocket:

mike_infra: I'll open an infra PR to add the 'keystore-proxy' service account role and IAM bindings for ephemeral erase tokens. Will also add a capability to mint ephemeral 'erase tokens' scoped to a single subject_id + TTL.

anya_privacy: Cross-region snapshot propagation: erase must mark snapshots for GC and also issue async purge jobs in other regions. Do we have an automated propagation workflow or is it manual?

sara_sec: We have an erase-propagation playbook but it's manual in places. I'll paste a short pseudo-runbook we can use to implement automation:

```
# pseudo-runbook for keystore-proxy erase
POST /v1/erase
payload: { "subject_id": "sub-123", "shards": ["s3://r1/...","s3://r2/..."], "manifest_signer": "keystore-proxy" }
# proxy steps:
- validate caller token + scope
- for each shard: call KMS -> decrypt metadata, zero metadata refs, issue delete to storage
- write signed manifest JSON to AuditDB (JWS signature using HSM key)
- forward manifest to cold-storage + index in AuditIndex
- queue snapshot-gc events for other regions
```

tom_oncall: Edge-case: if KMS returns 403 (missing key ACL) or 5xx, runbook says escalate to sec oncall and flag subject as 'freeze' to block further deletions until resolved. We should automate the freeze flag.

mike_infra: I'll add a 'freeze-user' boolean in the metadata service and check it in the proxy. PR #4827. If freeze=true, proxy returns HTTP 423 Locked and link to incident.

anya_privacy: Legal also wants a sample 'proof-of-erase' output they can attach to DSAR responses (PDF with signature metadata). Can proxy export the signed manifest + signature chain as a verifiable PDF?

sara_sec: Yes — manifest will be JWS over canonical JSON. We can provide a small tool to render manifest+signature into PDF with certificate chain and verification instructions. Legal can verify offline.

alex_legal: One more constraint: if there's a suspected data leak/vuln, do NOT perform irreversible erases until forensics snapshots are captured. We need a 'preservation hold' option during triage.

devops-bot: incident-bot: INC-2026-0099 created by sara_sec — hold any DSAR erases for subject sub-123 pending triage :warning:

mike_infra: Acknowledged. I'll add an incident guard in keystore-proxy and a redirect to the incident ticket in the 423 response.

anya_privacy: Timeline: infra PR by EOD, security to publish manifest schema + signature format by tomorrow, legal to confirm acceptable signature format. After that, we'll file a retention-exception for AuditDB cold-storage to keep manifests for 7 years.

alex_legal: Agreed — legal will prepare the retention-exception request and route to CISO for approval once implementation details are ready.

sara_sec: I'll kick off a short doc (internal) with schema, verification steps, and an example signed manifest. Also will add audit-forwarding to GCS cold with writelock.

mike_infra: I'll post the infra PR link here when ready.

anya_privacy: Thanks. If anyone spots a gap (RBAC/keystore/cross-region), call it out now.

sara_sec: One more: ensure the HSM key used for signing has an audit log of signing operations in KeyManager and key rotation policy documented. That proves chain-of-custody.

anya_privacy: Good point. We'll include that in the retention-exception justification.

alex_legal: Also keep a revocation list for manifests in case of accidental double-delete or manifest corruption — include manifest_id and reason.

mike_infra: Noted. I'll include manifest revocation table in AuditIndex schema.

anya_privacy: Great. I'll update DSAR runbook to reference these controls and ping security/infra for PRs.

sara_sec: :thumbsup:
